purpose: Machine-readable provenance for every file in launch-docs/assets/. Enforced by test/asset-provenance-gate.test.sh, which fails RED if any 'fixture' asset is referenced from a reader-facing surface (README.md, the npm README mirror, site/). A README reader never opens this directory's README, so the prose disclosure there cannot protect them on its own.

provenance_values.real: Every rendered datum came from this repo's actual state: real gate history, real team presence, real identities. Safe to embed on a reader-facing surface.
provenance_values.fixture: At least one rendered datum was seeded — invented teammates, a seeded verdict/beats file, a scratch workspace. The renderer is real; the data is not. NEVER safe to embed on a reader-facing surface.

fail_closed: The gate hardcodes 'fixture' as the default for any asset that is undeclared here or carries an unrecognised provenance value. That default lives in the test, NOT in this file — there is deliberately no manifest field that can widen what counts as 'real'. An unmarked asset is not assumed real.

assets.reason: A GENERATED placeholder, not a render of this repo's state, so it cannot be 'real' — the fail-closed default is the correct answer here. It is however the SAFEST possible fixture: it deliberately depicts no teammate, no handle, no verdict, no merge count and no file path, precisely because a fallback image of a bustling wall would repeat the wall.png/wall.json fabrication it exists alongside. Its entire rendered content is the words 'NO LIVE PRESENCE' and 'Static placeholder - this image is not a live wall.', which are true in both states it serves (roster empty, or control plane unreachable). It says nothing about a demo either: it also renders for a real dev whose real team is merely idle, and labelling their team a demo would be its own dishonesty - the demo label is a separate roster-triggered banner in the embed.
assets.receipt: Reproducible from source: `bin/heimdall-seed-demo-wall --emit-fallback-gif <path>` regenerates it, and that generator is the only place its pixels are defined - open it to see there is no teammate/verdict/count data to fabricate. test/demo-wall-honesty.test.sh asserts the rendered strings stay free of any teammate/verdict/count claim, and that the site copy is byte-identical to this one.

assets.reason: Source code, not rendered data - it has no name, number, or verdict of its own to fabricate. The standard-library-only builder and verifier of the pack: it reads the lattice, the palette and every cell out of the master's pixels and re-emits every derived file by integer scaling, so no pixel is blended and nothing is redrawn by eye. Byte-identical to hmdapp's assets/brand/gen-brand-pack.py.
assets.receipt: `python3 launch-docs/assets/gen-brand-pack.py build` leaves every file in this directory byte-identical (shasum before and after), and `verify` first feeds its own checkers a corrupted PNG, a wrong pixel and a broken SVG and requires each to be reported (the three `self-test` lines) before trusting any PASS it prints.

assets.reason: Source code, not rendered data - it has no name, number, or verdict of its own to fabricate. It runs gen-brand-pack.py build, then verify (a nonzero exit stops it), then compiles the iconset gen-brand-pack.py writes into hmd-mark.icns with iconutil. It never resamples: no `sips -z` and no `magick -resize`, because a smoothed pixel-art helm is a different, blurry logo. No seeded or invented pixels at any step.
assets.receipt: Re-running `./generate-logo-assets.sh` twice in a row produces byte-identical (shasum-matching) output for every file it writes, including hmd-mark.icns, and leaves `git status --short launch-docs/assets` empty: the pipeline is a pure function of the checked-in master.
